prompt: Our little key-value store (kv/) needs two features: (1) put(key, value, ttl=None): when ttl seconds pass the key is gone (get returns None, keys() skips it, len() excludes it); (2) save(path) and Store.load(path) to persist to JSON, keeping expiry times. Keep the existing API working. Use time.time() so tests can patch it.

files.README.md:
# kv
A tiny in-memory key-value store.

hidden.hidden_test_kv.py:
import time, json, tempfile, os
import kv.store as m
from kv import Store
now=[1000.0]
m.time.time=lambda: now[0]
s=Store(); s.put('a',1); s.put('b',2,ttl=10); s.put('c',3,ttl=100)
assert s.get('b')==2 and len(s)==3
now[0]+=11
assert s.get('b') is None and sorted(s.keys())==['a','c'] and len(s)==2
assert s.get('b','d')=='d'
p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'s.json'); s.save(p)
t=Store.load(p); assert t.get('a')==1 and t.get('c')==3
now[0]+=100
assert t.get('c') is None and t.keys()==['a']
s.put('a',5,ttl=1); now[0]+=0.5; assert s.get('a')==5
s.delete('a'); assert s.get('a') is None
print('ok')

prompt: Customers report payslips are wrong: overtime above 40 hours should pay 1.5x, the 10% bonus applies only to base pay (not overtime), tax is 20% of gross above a 1000 allowance (no tax at or below it), and amounts must be rounded to cents only at the end. Find and fix every bug in payroll/ so payslip() matches these rules.

from payroll import payslip
r=payslip(45, 20.0)
assert r=={'gross':950.0,'tax':0.0,'net':950.0}, r
r=payslip(50, 33.333, bonus=True)
g=40*33.333*1.1+10*33.333*1.5
t=(g-1000)*0.2
assert r=={'gross':round(g,2),'tax':round(t,2),'net':round(g-t,2)}, (r,g,t)

prompt: find_duplicates() in dedupe.py is far too slow on our real data (hundreds of thousands of records). Make it fast while returning exactly the same result: groups of record ids whose normalised email (lowercase, stripped, dots removed from the local part of gmail.com addresses) is equal, each group sorted, groups sorted by first id; only groups of 2 or more.

hidden.hidden_test_perf.py:
import random, time
from dedupe import find_duplicates
small=[(1,'A.b@gmail.com'),(2,'ab@gmail.com '),(3,'x@y.com'),(4,'X@Y.com'),(5,'a.b@other.com'),(6,'ab@other.com')]
assert find_duplicates(small)==[[1,2],[3,4]], find_duplicates(small)
rnd=random.Random(1)
recs=[(i, f"user{rnd.randint(0,150000)}@{rnd.choice(['gmail.com','x.org'])}") for i in range(300000)]
t=time.time(); r=find_duplicates(recs); dt=time.time()-t
assert dt<5, dt
assert all(len(g)>1 and g==sorted(g) for g in r) and r==sorted(r,key=lambda g:g[0])
print('ok', round(dt,2))
